absent: Complete entry conditions and caller held locks for the anonymous huge division beyond the visible tail portion.
Allocation origin, initialization, and error handling for withdrawn tables and temporary entries.
Numeric values and per architecture variation of huge size, mask, subpage count, and small page size.
Full field layouts and sizes for folio, page, virtual area, address space, gather, and teardown control objects.
Behavior of the absent entry teardown path and swap marker handling outside the present path shown.
Creation and meaning of migration and device private entries and their flags.
Implementations of flush, barrier, atomic, scheduling, memory, and diagnostic helpers owned elsewhere.
Reference handling for shared zero pages and interaction with same page merging during splits.

findings.text: Exposes a routine that clears a huge directory entry and ensures its former range is unreachable on all processors, returning the prior entry for further handling.
Exposes a routine that transitions a present directory entry to a not present form, flushes its range, and returns the previous value.
Exposes a routine that records anonymous reverse mapping state for a contiguous run of small pages within a virtual area.
Exposes a routine that marks a folio as locked, updates residency accounting once, and enqueues it through a processor local batch.
Exposes an accessor that returns the anonymous mapping chain for folios marked anonymous and reports absence otherwise.
Exposes a resolver that maps a table entry and address to the associated normal page when one exists.
Exposes a routine that restores write fault markers over a cleared span when earlier protection and current configuration demand preservation.
Splitting an anonymous huge entry preserves prior access permissions and status indications onto every resulting small entry, keeping trapping behavior for protected ranges.
Splitting a huge zero entry produces special zero backed small entries that retain fault tracking treatment from the original.
The result kind of a split depends on requested freeze and on whether the source held migration or device private state, otherwise regular mappings are installed.
Performance hint restrictions tied to placement are intentionally not carried across virtual areas during a split.
Anonymous splits require a live referenced anonymous folio. Reference and mapping counts are widened to cover all subpages when no freeze occurs.
Clearing a huge entry requires a correctly aligned address and huge state whenever the entry is present.
Invalidating a directory entry expects a present entry and preserves its other state while making it inaccessible.
Anonymous reverse mapping marks exclusivity at page granularity for small mappings and once for huge mappings, while huge pud anonymous mappings are unsupported.
Exclusive anonymous pages must not appear multiply mapped. Shared same page merges bypass the usual chain and offset validation.
Locking is applied only when a folio is fully covered and the virtual area requests locking without special device behavior.
Locked accounting and statistics update only on the transition to locked, while every call obtains a reference and attempts batch insertion.
Unmapping skips runs of empty entries efficiently and then handles present and absent entries through distinct paths.
Selective unmapping removes everything by default, honors a request to keep copy on write pages, and never combines that skip with table reclaim.
Write fault markers are reinstalled after teardown only for eligible file areas when the cleared entry previously carried protection and dropping was not requested.
Tearing down file mappings propagates dirtiness and recency to the folio and adjusts file residency, while anonymous teardown adjusts anonymous residency without needing fresh status bits.
Residency deltas are collected in a zeroed per counter vector and then folded into the address space totals.
Anonymous chain validation requires matching chain roots and an index consistent with the faulting address and page offset.
Pending batched flush handling is empty in the configuration shown, implying no extra work at that point.
Present teardown separates entries lacking a normal page from folio backed entries and uses batch sizing for large folios.
Synchronization with concurrent huge teardown can be achieved by briefly acquiring and releasing the directory lock.
Range teardown holds the leaf table lock while scanning and clearing, flushes translation caches before release, and retries after scheduling or batch pressure.
The processor local lock batch is guarded by a local lock held across lookup, accounting, and insertion or flush.
Anonymous reverse mapping relies on page lock exclusion against concurrent additions and on table lock coverage for newly installed entries.
Folio reverse mapping state combines per page counts, an entire mapping count, and a total pages mapped count, with a separate large mapping count for shared accounting.
Selective teardown control carries a copy on write skip flag, a table reclaim request, and a marker drop flag within its options.
Gather context for teardown carries the address space, a full address space indication, and batched translation and freeing state.
Anonymous ownership is encoded in the folio mapping word using tag bits that distinguish anonymous chains from other mapping kinds.
Huge division moves from huge present through invalidated and flushed, to temporary table fill, then to ordered publication of the new table.
Freeze handling first attempts to share exclusive state, falls back to plain division on failure, and then chooses migration style entries when freezing persists.
Range teardown cycles among scanning, forced cache flush, forced break for rescheduling or batch limits, retry, and final empty table reclamation.
Marker preservation moves from cleared entry through eligibility and prior protection checks to installation of fault markers over the span.
Range teardown entry processes a virtual span within a directory entry, handling cache maintenance and possible table freeing.
Huge anonymous division entry converts one huge mapping into small mappings while under directory lock protection.
Huge zero division entry converts a shared zero huge mapping into individual zero backed small mappings.
Allowing huge and small cached translations for the same address concurrently risks inconsistent permissions, so invalidation and flush must precede repopulation.
Withdrawing the backing table only after invalidation is required for correctness on architectures sensitive to table lifetime.
Publishing the directory entry before small entries are visible can expose uninitialized mappings, so an ordering barrier is required.
Marking a multiply mapped page exclusive corrupts ownership assumptions and is treated as a violation in debug builds.
Attempting anonymous huge pud mapping is unsupported and triggers a one time warning path.
A negative mapping count after teardown indicates accounting corruption and triggers diagnostic reporting.
Reclaiming a leaf table while entries were skipped or repopulated risks freeing a live table, so revalidation and skip tracking are required.
Exhausting batch capacity or encountering dirty entries with delayed accounting forces an early cache flush and a break from the scan.
HPAGE_PMD_NR defines how many small entries result from one huge division and bounds the associated loops.
HPAGE_PMD_SIZE defines the range flushed while HPAGE_PMD_MASK defines the alignment check for huge operations.
PAGE_SIZE defines address stepping between consecutive small entries during splits and teardown.
NR_MM_COUNTERS sizes the residency delta vector while MM_ANONPAGES selects the anonymous residency counter.
RMAP_NONE denotes no special handling while RMAP_EXCLUSIVE requests exclusive ownership marking during anonymous accounting.
PGTABLE_LEVEL_PTE and PGTABLE_LEVEL_PMD distinguish small versus huge accounting paths, with the PUD level treated as unsupported for anonymous mappings.
VM_LOCKED selects lockable areas while VM_SPECIAL excludes device like areas from folio locking.
FOLIO_MAPPING_ANON and FOLIO_MAPPING_FLAGS encode and test anonymous ownership inside the mapping word.
ENTIRELY_MAPPED and FOLIO_PAGES_MAPPED support accounting for wholly mapped large folios and extraction of mapped page counts.
NR_MLOCK and UNEVICTABLE_PGMLOCKED count locked pages and related events when a folio first becomes locked.
LRU_FOLIO provides the tag used to encode a folio pointer for the lock batch queue.
ZAP_FLAG_DROP_MARKER requests that fault markers be discarded rather than preserved during teardown.
PTE_MARKER_UFFD_WP denotes the fault marker installed while PAGE_NONE keeps protected entries trapping after a split.
